name: @wootsup/apimapper-mcp

tools.name: apimapper_rest_modules_status
tools.description: Module-loading status for this MCP adapter (which sub-modules registered cleanly). For runtime connectivity + auth checks against the API Mapper REST surface, use apimapper_health.

tools.name: apimapper_health
tools.description:
Check connectivity + auth against the API Mapper REST namespace. Returns {wp_base, auth, connectivity, connection_count, http_status, apimapper_api_status}. `apimapper_api_status` reports the downstream api.wootsup.com health (OK/HTTP N/timeout/unreachable) so a degradation of getimo infra is distinguishable from a customer-server issue. Run this first if any other tool fails.

Example:
  apimapper_health({})

tools.name: apimapper_connection_list
tools.description:
List API Mapper connections — a LEAN projection by default (id / name / source / host / health). The default limit of 25 already covers a typical install — most customers run with 5-25 connections, increase the limit only if you have a specific reason to expect more. Pass `fields: ['all']` for the full dump (endpoint URL, method, auth_type, credential_id), or a list of specific extra columns. Use apimapper_advanced_read({ tool: "apimapper_connection_get", arguments: { id } }) for full details of a single connection.

Example:
  apimapper_connection_list({})  // lean projection, up to 25 connections
  apimapper_connection_list({ source: 'user' })  // narrow to user-created only
  apimapper_connection_list({ fields: ['all'] })  // full detail dump

limit.description: Max items (1-500). Default 25 already covers a typical install — do not raise unless you have evidence the list is larger.

fields.description: Opt into extra columns. Omit for the lean default (id/name/source/host/health). Pass ['all'] for the full dump (endpoint URL, method, auth_type, credential_id).

name_query.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on connection name. Applied in-memory after the upstream fetch — does NOT change the REST query. Must be 2+ characters; single-char probes are blocked. Combine with `source` for narrower results.

include_meta.description: Include the Rich-Card `_meta` payload (a base64 block appended to the table text) in the response. Default false (lean output; no MCP host this ships to renders it). Set to true to opt in; the human-readable table text is unaffected either way.

tools.name: apimapper_connection_create
tools.description:
Create a custom connection. **Use ONLY when no library template matches your target API.** First call `apimapper_library_featured()` or `apimapper_library_list({ search: '<api-name>' })` (min 3 chars) — Google Sheets, Calendly, Notion, Airtable, GitHub, Pexels, Unsplash, OpenWeatherMap, REST Countries, Google Drive/Docs/Slides/Tasks all have ready-to-use templates with auto-configured auth and field-detection. Library activation via `apimapper_library_activate({ id })` is the canonical customer path; connection_create is the fallback for niche or unknown APIs. The server enforces this: a custom create on an API already covered by a curated template is blocked with a 409 naming the template to activate — pass `acknowledge_no_library: true` to intentionally override that block. The guard matches on the request HOST against the curated library; a connection to an uncovered host is NEVER blocked and needs no `acknowledge_no_library` — only set that flag AFTER you actually receive a 409.

Note: connection auth_type spellings differ from apimapper_credential_create's: here it is `basic` / `oauth2`, whereas credential_create uses `basic_auth` / `oauth2_code` / `oauth2_cc`. Use the spelling for the tool you are calling.

Secrets live in a credential (`credential_id`): a value typed into the endpoint, a parameter, header or template field under a name that is a secret whatever the API (password, passphrase, token, api_key, client_secret, Authorization), or a [REDACTED] copied from connection_get is refused (422 `secret_outside_credential` / `redacted_value_without_stored_value`). An ambiguous name (key, appid, sid, session_key, client_id) is saved.

`template_fields` takes connection values: each `{{placeholder}}` of the base URL (the origin of `endpoint`) needs its example value there, or the create is refused. A placeholder in the endpoint path or query is a node value: it fills no request from here and may be refused with `invalid_arguments`; set it per source in apimapper_flow_setup_with_sources `template_fields`, or give it a starting value in `starting_values`. Built-in tokens (`{{__today}}`, `{{__today_date}}`, `{{__this_year}}` ...) are filled when the request runs and take none. A refusal lists every reason in `validation_errors`, not only the one `error_code` names.

Example:
  apimapper_connection_create({ name: 'Pexels API', endpoint: 'https://api.pexels.com/v1/search', method: 'GET', auth_type: 'bearer', items_path: 'photos' })
  apimapper_connection_create({ name: 'Shop', endpoint: 'https://{{shop}}.example.com/v1/products', template_fields: { shop: 'demo' } })
  apimapper_connection_create({ name: 'Forecast', endpoint: 'https://api.example.com/forecast?date={{date}}', starting_values: { date: '{{__today_date}}' } })

endpoint.description: Endpoint path or full URL (e.g., "https://api.example.com/posts"). It becomes the connection's one endpoint in endpoints[], named after the connection.

auth_type.description: Auth type (snake_case wire key). NB: credential_create spells these `basic_auth` (here `basic`) and `oauth2_code`/`oauth2_cc` (here `oauth2`).

credential_id.description: Credential ID (snake_case wire key) if auth_type requires one

items_path.description: JSONPath to items array (snake_case wire key)

items_shape.description: Row shape of the answer at items_path: 'flat' (a list of objects, used as it is; the default), 'parallel_arrays' (an object of equal-length lists {"time":[...],"temp":[...]}, zipped into one row per position), 'wrapped_object' (an object holding one list {"events":[...]}, that list), 'single_object' (one object, one row), 'headers_rows' (a 2D array [[h1,h2],[v1,v2]] as Google Sheets returns it, one row per line named by the first line).

default_params.description: Extra query parameters every request sends, keyed by name, e.g. { units: 'metric' }; a built-in token is filled when the request runs. Not the starting value of a {{placeholder}}: that goes in starting_values.

starting_values.description: starting_values: { placeholder: value } sets the starting value of a {{placeholder}} in an endpoint path or query, sent when neither the flow node nor the page element sets one; a built-in token such as {{__today_date}} is filled when the request runs. Not on a library connection (its template sets them).

cache_ttl.description: Cache TTL in seconds (snake_case wire key)

template_fields.description: Example value for each {{placeholder}} of the base URL, keyed by name, e.g. { "shop": "demo" }. A placeholder in the endpoint path or query is a node value and fills no request from here.

acknowledge_no_library.description: Set true ONLY when no library template fits and you intentionally need a custom connection. The server blocks custom creates on APIs that already have a curated library template; this flag is the audited override. Prefer apimapper_library_activate({ id }) when a template exists.

summary.description: Optional one-line summary of this change for the change history (e.g., "Added a Pexels photo connection").

tools.name: apimapper_connection_data
tools.description:
Fetch sample data from a connection's configured endpoint. The PHP handler reads ALL query params as source-context for template substitution. Use `limit`/`offset` to trim the response items in-memory — this does NOT trigger multi-page fetch upstream (the request is single-shot). Use `fields` to project each item down to a whitelist of leaf keys, cutting response size on sparse queries.

If a library/template connection returns a 'Please configure the required fields' diagnostic, the missing values are TEMPLATE FIELDS — supply them here via `template_fields` (e.g., { spreadsheet_id: '…' }) rather than re-creating the connection or starting a new OAuth flow. A connection whose template_fields are already resolved IS configured; inspect them with apimapper_advanced_read({ tool: "apimapper_connection_get", arguments: { id } }).

Example:
  apimapper_connection_data({ id: 'con_abc123', limit: 10 })  // first 10 items
  apimapper_connection_data({ id: 'con_abc123', limit: 5, offset: 10 })  // skip 10, take 5
  apimapper_connection_data({ id: 'con_abc123', fields: ['title', 'image.url'] })  // 2 leaf keys per item
  apimapper_connection_data({ id: 'con_abc123', template_fields: { query: 'nature' } })

id.description: Connection ID. Use apimapper_connection_list to find.

endpoint.description: Named endpoint SELECTION — NOT a URL. This is the label of a configured endpoint on the connection (e.g., "Scheduled Events", "Get Values"), the same names connection_create exposes as endpoints[]. List them via apimapper_advanced_read({ tool: "apimapper_connection_get", arguments: { id } }). Empty-string and whitespace-only values are rejected at the schema boundary to prevent "?endpoint=" query garbage; omit the field entirely to use the connection default.

template_fields.description: Template field values flattened into the query string. Accepts string/number/boolean values; non-string values are stringified via JS String() (number 25 → "25", true → "true", false → "false"). A list is sent as one text with commas (["a","b"] → "a,b"). NaN/Infinity numbers are rejected by schema (defense-in-depth). Nested objects are rejected. Example: { spreadsheet_id: "abc", per_page: 25, active: true } → ?spreadsheet_id=abc&per_page=25&active=true

limit.description: Trim the returned items array to at most N (1-500). Applied in-memory after the upstream fetch — does NOT request fewer items from the source API. Omit to return the full response.

offset.description: Skip the first N items before applying `limit`. Applied in-memory. Useful for inspecting later items in a large response when combined with `limit`.

fields.description: Optional whitelist of fields to keep per item (supports nested paths like 'image.url'). Default: all fields. Cuts response size on sparse queries — e.g. fields:['title','image.url'] keeps only those two leaf keys per record.

tools.name: apimapper_credential_list
tools.description:
List all stored credentials (sanitised — secrets omitted). The `auth_type` parameter is a CLIENT-SIDE filter — the server returns the same set regardless of `auth_type`. Calling repeatedly with different `auth_type` values returns identical underlying data; a single call returns everything. Use apimapper_advanced_read({ tool: "apimapper_credential_get", arguments: { id } }) for one credential's full metadata.

Example:
  apimapper_credential_list({})  // returns all credentials
  apimapper_credential_list({ auth_type: 'oauth2_code' })  // local filter only

auth_type.description: Filter by auth_type (server wire-format field). Applied CLIENT-SIDE after the server returns all credentials — calling with different values does NOT change what the server returns.

include_meta.description: Include the Rich-Card `_meta` payload (a base64 block appended to the table text) in the response. Default false (lean output; no MCP host this ships to renders it). Set to true to opt in; the human-readable table text is unaffected either way.

tools.name: apimapper_oauth_authorize_begin
tools.description:
Initiate the OAuth2 authorization-code flow for a credential. Returns the upstream authorize URL the user must visit in a browser to grant consent, plus the `redirect_uri` this site receives the callback on. After consent: call apimapper_advanced_read({ tool: "apimapper_credential_get", arguments: { id } }) to verify the credential was populated. If `credential_id` is omitted, supply `provider` to scope the lookup — when exactly one OAuth credential matches it is used automatically; when several match the user is asked to pick. For a CUSTOM provider not in the catalog, pass `oauth_config` (authorization_url / token_url / scopes / use_pkce) together with `client_id` / `client_secret` and an optional `credential_name` — no pre-existing credential is needed. IMPORTANT: add the returned `redirect_uri` to the provider's allowed redirect URIs BEFORE opening `authorize_url`, or consent will fail.

Example:
  apimapper_oauth_authorize_begin({ credential_id: 'cred_google_drive' })
  apimapper_oauth_authorize_begin({ provider: 'google' })  // resolves by provider
  apimapper_oauth_authorize_begin({ oauth_config: { authorization_url: 'https://x/authorize', token_url: 'https://x/token' }, client_id: 'cid', client_secret: 'sec', credential_name: 'My App' })

credential_id.description: Credential ID (must be type oauth2_code). Use apimapper_credential_list. Omit to resolve by `provider` instead.

provider.description: OAuth provider slug to resolve the credential when `credential_id` is omitted (e.g., "google"). Matched case-insensitively against the credential's oauth_provider, then provider; a Google or Microsoft account credential serves every service of that account.

oauth_config.description: Custom-provider OAuth config (omit for catalog providers / existing credentials). Pass with client_id / client_secret to start consent for a self-described provider.

client_id.description: OAuth client_id for a custom `oauth_config` flow.

client_secret.description: OAuth client_secret for a custom `oauth_config` flow (encrypted server-side; never echoed back).

credential_name.description: Display name for the credential created after consent (custom `oauth_config` flow).

tools.name: apimapper_library_list
tools.description:
List connection templates shipping with API Mapper. The catalog is small (~30-50 templates) — a SINGLE CALL without filters returns the full set in one round-trip. Do NOT iterate per category and do NOT probe with short search strings; call apimapper_advanced_read({ tool: "apimapper_library_categories", arguments: {} }) first if you need an overview of available slugs, then filter the table you already have client-side.

Server-side filters (sent as query params, server returns pre-filtered):
  - category: narrow by category slug (e.g. 'media', 'productivity')
  - search:   substring match on template name/description

Client-side filters (applied AFTER fetch in this MCP process):
  - provider:  narrow by upstream provider (e.g. 'google', 'meta')
  - activated: narrow to currently-activated or not-activated

Implication: When combined with `limit`, the total reflects the post-server filter — if you set limit:50 + provider:meta and the server returns 50 mixed-provider items, you may see <50 after the client filter. Re-call with a higher limit or omit the client-side filter to see the full server-side result.

Examples:
  apimapper_library_list({})  // returns the whole catalog
  apimapper_library_list({ category: 'media' })  // narrow to one category (server-side)
  apimapper_library_list({ provider: 'google', limit: 200 })  // raise limit because provider filter is client-side

category.description: Filter by category slug. Use apimapper_advanced_read({ tool: "apimapper_library_categories", arguments: {} }) to discover slugs — do NOT loop over every category, the result of an unfiltered list({}) already covers them all.

search.description: Free-text search. Must be 3+ characters — single-char probes are blocked because the catalog is too small to need typeahead.

page.description: Pagination page (1-based). Capped at 2 — the catalog rarely fills more than one page at the default limit, iterating further yields empty results.

limit.description: Max items per page (1-500). The default of 100 already exceeds the full catalog — increase only if you have a specific reason.

include_meta.description: Include the Rich-Card `_meta` payload (a base64 block appended to the table text) in the response. Default false (lean output; no MCP host this ships to renders it). Set to true to opt in; the human-readable table text is unaffected either way.

tools.name: apimapper_library_featured
tools.description:
List the curated, featured connection templates — the MANDATORY first call before building any new API integration. Use this to discover whether a ready-made template (with OAuth wizard, auto-header detection, and a curated YOOtheme schema) already exists for the API you need. Keywords: featured, recommended, starter, popular templates, pre-built, catalog landing. When NOT to use: to search the WHOLE catalog by name use apimapper_library_list; to read one template's full contract use apimapper_library_connection_detail({ id }); only fall back to apimapper_connection_create when no template matches.

Example:
  apimapper_library_featured({})

include_meta.description: Include the Rich-Card `_meta` payload (a base64 block appended to the table text) in the response. Default false (lean output; no MCP host this ships to renders it). Set to true to opt in; the human-readable table text is unaffected either way.

tools.name: apimapper_library_connection_detail
tools.description:
Fetch the full connection template (endpoints, default_params, auth scheme) for one library item.

Example:
  apimapper_library_connection_detail({ id: 'pexels' })

id.description: Library item ID. Use apimapper_library_list to find.

tools.name: apimapper_library_activate
tools.description:
Activate a library template: creates a new connection, or returns an existing one of the same template, credential (or none) and configuration (status `reused`, or `reused_healed` when it was repaired; `force_new: true` creates another). 

**FOR AUTH-PROTECTED TEMPLATES (most APIs incl. Google Sheets, Notion, Airtable, Pexels, OpenWeatherMap, Calendly, GitHub):** you MUST link a credential. A credential fits when its provider is the template's (one Google or Microsoft account credential serves every service of that account) and its auth type matches; a credential without a provider fits none. The tool auto-links when exactly ONE credential fits; otherwise it fails with `credential_required` or `credential_ambiguous`. An explicit `credential_id` of another provider or auth type is refused with `credential_mismatch`. Pre-flight: call `apimapper_credential_list({})` and confirm a credential exists for the provider — if not, create one via `apimapper_oauth_authorize_begin` (OAuth) or `apimapper_advanced({tool:'apimapper_credential_create',arguments:{…, provider}})` (api_key/bearer). 

**`extra_fields` takes connection values only:** the `{{placeholders}}` of the template's base URL, e.g. strapi / woocommerce `site_url`. A value an endpoint path or query reads (google-sheets `spreadsheet_id` and `range`, google-docs `document_id`, a region, a search term) is a node value: it fills no request from here and may be refused with `invalid_arguments`; set it per source in apimapper_flow_setup_with_sources `template_fields`. apimapper_library_connection_detail({ id }) shows the base URL and the fields of any template.

**Picker fields**: once the credential is stored, list the choices with apimapper_advanced_read({ tool: 'apimapper_connection_resources', arguments: { library_id, credential_id, field } }). Only fields whose template declares a picker list choices. A picked id goes where its field belongs: a base URL field into `extra_fields` here, a node field into the source's `template_fields` in apimapper_flow_setup_with_sources.

⚠️ Template fields passed at the TOP LEVEL of the call are silently ignored (the schema strips unknown keys) — they MUST be nested under `extra_fields` (F186).

Examples:
  apimapper_library_activate({ id: 'pexels', credential_id: 'cred_pexels' })
  apimapper_library_activate({ id: 'woocommerce', extra_fields: { site_url: 'shop.example.com' } })  // auto-links the unique matching credential

id.description: Library item ID. Use apimapper_library_list to find.

credential_id.description: Credential ID. REQUIRED for auth-protected templates unless exactly one credential of the template's provider and auth type exists (then auto-linked); one of another provider is refused with credential_mismatch. Use apimapper_credential_list({}) to find one, or apimapper_oauth_authorize_begin({provider}) to create one.

extra_fields.description: Connection values: the {{placeholders}} of the template's base URL, e.g. { site_url: "shop.example.com" } for strapi or woocommerce. A value an endpoint path or query reads is a node value and fills no request from here; set it in apimapper_flow_setup_with_sources `template_fields`. Read the fields via apimapper_library_connection_detail({ id }).

library_connection.description: Optional template metadata override (rename connection, override base_url, etc.). REST key: library_connection.

force_new.description: Force creation of a NEW connection even if a matching one exists (default: false → the backend reuses a healthy connection of the same template, credential (or none) and configuration). Set true for a second connection of the same template, with or without a credential. REST key: force_new.

tools.name: apimapper_yootheme_binding_for_flow
tools.description:
Bridge tool: given a published flow id, return the EXACT YOOtheme GraphQL source names (singular + List) and the schema fields available for binding. Replaces a 3-call chain (flow_get → parse schema JSON → yt-builder sources_list grep) with one deterministic call.

Use after `apimapper_flow_full_recompile_publish` to discover what to bind. In yt-builder-mcp, bind directly with yootheme_builder_element_bind_source({ layout_id, element_path, source_name, field_mappings, etag }) (a first-class tool in tools/list since F116; on pre-F116 server builds it is reachable via yootheme_builder_advanced({ tool: "yootheme_builder_element_bind_source", arguments: {…} })).

The `source_name_list` is the canonical Multi-Items target (grid/list/slider containers). The `source_name_single` is the FLAT top-level Single field — bind it to a standalone leaf (headline / hero / one stat) with a FLAT field name. The `source_name_singular` is the wrapper object; its dotted singular.<field> nested path is metadata-less and renders blank, so prefer `source_name_single` for single bindings. `source_label_list` and `source_label_single` are the names the Builder's source picker shows for them (compiled flows).

`related_source` names the per-item relation (label, placeholders, placeholder_defaults: the default of each placeholder that has one) that YOOtheme offers as a Multiple items source on templates and pages; null when the flow is not compiled, has a shortcode output, or is a single item without placeholders.

`ready_for_binding` says the published schema can be bound. `rows_last_run` is how many rows the last recorded run delivered (null: no run since the last publish, or an error run; a trace through apimapper_advanced_read records one); `warnings` names a list source whose last run delivered exactly one row.

F158 CAVEAT: `example_field_mappings` are HEURISTIC prop keys (title/content/meta/image/link) computed WITHOUT knowing the target element's real prop set — a grid_item, headline or list_item each expose DIFFERENT props. Call yt-builder `yootheme_builder_element_type_get_schema` for the target element FIRST and bind only props that element actually renders; an unknown prop key binds to nothing (silent blank, no error).

Example:
  apimapper_yootheme_binding_for_flow({ id: 'flow_VYvfwySM34fypAbDoc7rx' })

id.description: Flow ID (e.g., "flow_VYvfwySM34fypAbDoc7rx"). Use apimapper_advanced_read({ tool: "apimapper_flow_list", arguments: {} }) to find.

tools.name: apimapper_flow_setup_with_sources
tools.description:
Compose a complete flow from connections AND/OR CMS-native local sources in one call. Sequence: (1) build graph via buildFlowGraph() — pure function, deterministic layout. (2) POST /flows (creates row). (3) POST /flows/{id}/compile (publishes to YOOtheme). Returns flow_id + per-step status. On partial failure, returns cleanup hint. Each source is EITHER an API connection (`connection`) OR a local source (`local_source: { content_type, limit?, filters? }`) — never both. Local content_type must be fully-qualified (e.g. 'wordpress/post', 'joomla/article'); a bare 'post' is rejected at save time. A connection that a library activation just created may carry a flow of its own, still untouched: this call then REPLACES that flow's graph instead of creating one (`created: false`, `reused_activation_flow`), takes over one such flow per call, and names the others it left (`kept_activation_flows`).

Connection-source example:
  apimapper_flow_setup_with_sources({ name: 'Pexels + IG Gallery', sources: [{ connection: 'con_pexels', endpoint: 'ep_photos' }, { connection: 'con_instagram', endpoint: 'ep_media' }], merge: { strategy: 'concat' }, output: { type: 'yootheme', name: 'Gallery' } })

Local-source example:
  apimapper_flow_setup_with_sources({ name: 'Latest Posts', sources: [{ local_source: { content_type: 'wordpress/post', limit: 12 } }], output: { type: 'yootheme', name: 'Posts' } })

Filter example (one-shot — no raw graph editing needed):
  apimapper_flow_setup_with_sources({ name: 'Warm EU Cities', sources: [{ connection: 'con_weather', endpoint: 'ep_current' }], filter: { field: 'temp', operator: 'gt', value: 10 }, output: { type: 'yootheme', name: 'Warm' } })

Filter operators: equals, not_equals, contains, starts_with, ends_with, gt, gte, lt, lte, exists, not_exists, empty, not_empty, in, not_in. Use the named operators (gt/lt), NOT symbols (>/<). Numeric operators auto-coerce formatted strings ('$1,250,000'). The filter runs AFTER merge and BEFORE transform.

Multi-stage reshape? Pass `transform` as an ARRAY of stages — each stage gets its own depth budget.

Multi-transform example (JMESPath depth cap → split into chained transforms):
  apimapper_flow_setup_with_sources({ name: 'Opening Hours', sources: [{ connection: 'con_hours', endpoint: 'ep_hours' }], transform: [{ expression: '[1:]' }, { expression: '[*].{day: [0], hours: [1]}' }], output: { type: 'yootheme', name: 'Hours' } })

Formatted placeholder example (one source):
  apimapper_flow_setup_with_sources({ name: 'Forecast', sources: [{ connection: 'con_weather', endpoint: 'ep_forecast', template_fields: { date: 'today' }, placeholder_formats: { date: { id: 'date-format', config: { format: 'Y-m-d' } } } }], output: { name: 'Forecast' } })

Chained sources example (one source fills another's placeholders):
  apimapper_flow_setup_with_sources({ name: 'Weather', sources: [{ connection: 'con_geo', endpoint: 'ep_search', label: 'Geocoding', template_fields: { name: 'Berlin' } }, { connection: 'con_archive', endpoint: 'ep_daily', chains: { lat: { from: 'Geocoding', path: 'latitude' }, lon: { from: 'Geocoding', path: 'longitude' } } }], output: { name: 'Weather', field_formats: { weather_code: { id: 'map-values', config: { entries: [{ from: '0', to: 'Clear sky' }, { from: '61', to: 'Rain' }], fallback: 'keep' } } } } })
A chain reads the first row of the `from` source; that source is not merged. Chain and format names are the source's values: path and query placeholders and query parameters, never a base-URL placeholder. Placeholder formats: date-format, map-values. Field formats: map-values, pattern-link, relative-timestamp. Details: apimapper_get_skill({ topic: 'getting-started', full: true }), section 'Chains and formats'.
Pass `transform` as an ARRAY to chain N transform nodes (t1 → t2 → …). The pipe between chained nodes resets the JMESPath depth counter, so a reshape that overflows the depth cap (10) in one expression succeeds when split across two. A single `{ expression }` object still works for the one-transform case.

connection.description: Connection ID (API source). Use apimapper_connection_list to find.

local_source.description: Local-source descriptor (CMS-native source). Mutually exclusive with `connection`.

content_type.description: Fully-qualified content type, e.g. "wordpress/post", "wordpress/page", "joomla/article". The bare "post" is rejected at save time — always qualify with the platform prefix.

limit.description: Max items (clamped to tier max server-side)

endpoint.description: The endpoint to read, by its key (e.g., "ep_photos"; apimapper_advanced_read({ tool: "apimapper_connection_get", arguments: { id } }) lists them). Required when the connection has several endpoints: without it nothing is created.

template_fields.description: Values of the endpoint path and query placeholders (e.g., {"spreadsheet_id":"...","range":"A1:D20"}). A value that takes several entries (a multi_select field) also takes a list, e.g. {"daily":["weather_code","temperature_2m_max"]}. A base-URL value is set on the connection (apimapper_advanced({ tool: "apimapper_connection_update", arguments: { id, patch } })), not here.

label.description: Display label for the source node

chains.description: Placeholders filled from another source's first row, keyed by placeholder name. The source named in `from` only supplies values; it is not merged into the output.

from.description: The source that supplies the value: its label, or its position in sources (0 = first)

path.description: Field in that source's first row, e.g. "latitude"

placeholder_formats.description: Format a placeholder's value before it is sent, keyed by placeholder name

config.description: Format settings (* = required): date-format {format, input_format, relative}; map-values {entries*: [{from, to}], fallback: keep|empty|text, fallback_text}; pattern-link {pattern*, url_template*, link_class, target, rel}; relative-timestamp {output: text|number, unit: minutes|hours|days}

sources.description: 1..N sources — each a connection source OR a local_source (CMS-native)

joinKey.description: Left-side join key field (required for strategy=join). This is the field PRESENT IN BOTH sources' rows on which they join. DISCOVER it first: call apimapper_connection_data on EACH source and find a field whose values overlap and are the SAME type/format on both sides (a string "P-100" never equals a number 42). If the keys differ in shape, add a Transform before the merge to make them comparable (e.g. date-primitive transforms for a weekday name ↔ ISO date). See apimapper_get_skill({ topic: 'merge-two-sources-on-key' }) → 'Discovering the join key'.

joinKeyRight.description: Right-side join key field (defaults to joinKey). Set this when the two sources name the same value differently (e.g. left 'property_id' vs right 'propertyId'). Sample both with apimapper_connection_data to confirm the values actually match.

filter.description: Optional Filter node (F54). Inline `{field, operator, value}` or `{conditions:[...], logic}`. Runs after merge, before transform. Unknown operators are rejected hard.

operator.description: Comparison operator. Numeric: gt/gte/lt/lte. Text: equals/not_equals/contains/starts_with/ends_with. Set: in/not_in. Presence: exists/not_exists/empty/not_empty. Symbolic operators (">", "<") are NOT accepted — use "gt"/"lt".

value.description: Value to compare against. Omit for value-less operators (exists/not_exists/empty/not_empty; for empty/not_empty, 0 and '0' are NOT empty). Numeric operators auto-coerce formatted strings like "$1,250,000".

transform.description: Optional Transform node(s). Multi-stage reshape? Pass `transform` as an ARRAY of stages — each stage gets its own depth budget. A single `{ expression }` covers the one-reshape case; an ARRAY CHAINs multiple transforms (t1 → t2 → …). Chaining is the remedy for the JMESPath depth cap (10): split one over-nested expression into two shallow ones — the pipe between chained nodes resets the depth counter. See apimapper_get_skill({ topic: 'jmespath-cookbook' }) → 'Two-Transform split'.

name.description: Name stored on the Output node; the YOOtheme dropdown shows the flow `name`

field_formats.description: Format an output field, keyed by field name (e.g. {"code":{"id":"map-values","config":{...}}})

config.description: Format settings (* = required): date-format {format, input_format, relative}; map-values {entries*: [{from, to}], fallback: keep|empty|text, fallback_text}; pattern-link {pattern*, url_template*, link_class, target, rel}; relative-timestamp {output: text|number, unit: minutes|hours|days}

summary.description: Optional one-line summary of this flow for the change history (e.g., "Set up a merged Pexels + Instagram gallery").

compile.description: Compile after save (= publish to YOOtheme)

autofix.description: Defaults to true. When compile:true, auto-repair empty-output-schema compile errors by calling detect-schema then retrying compile so the new source compiles and appears. Pass false to opt out (verbatim old behaviour — no detect-schema retry). Mirrors `flow_full_recompile_publish` autofix.

tools.name: apimapper_flow_full_recompile_publish
tools.description:
Compile a flow + invalidate admin cache + flush the YOOtheme schema cache in one call. Use after upstream API changes to ensure the flow + schema are fresh. Each step's success is surfaced separately, and a cache-clear failure does NOT silently downgrade compile success. autofix defaults to true: it auto-repairs common compile errors (empty output schema → re-detect; then retry compile) AND flushes the YOOtheme schema cache so the source becomes visible in the YOOtheme builder — no second MCP package needed. Pass autofix:false to opt out (compile + admin-cache only, no detect-schema retry, no YT flush — the verbatim v2.0.7 behaviour).

Example:
  apimapper_flow_full_recompile_publish({ id: 'flow_Z2fLg70M84' })

id.description: Flow ID. Use apimapper_advanced_read({ tool: "apimapper_flow_list", arguments: {} }) to find.

autofix.description: When true (default): on empty-schema compile error, call detect-schema and retry compile. On compile success, also flush the YOOtheme schema cache so the source surfaces in the YOOtheme builder. Pass false to opt out — compile + admin-cache only, no detect-schema retry, no YT flush (the verbatim v2.0.7 behaviour).

summary.description: Optional one-line summary of this publish for the change history (e.g., "Republished after refreshing the upstream schema").

tools.name: apimapper_onboarding
tools.description:
ONE-SHOT BRIEFING — run this FIRST when meeting a new install. Aggregates site platform, license tier, connections, flows, and a complete library brief (total_count + categories + featured + popular + free-text hint) into a single response. After this call you have full orientation; do NOT chain apimapper_advanced_read({ tool: "apimapper_library_categories", arguments: {} }) or apimapper_library_list to rediscover what is already in the report. Tolerates partial failures and never throws.

Example:
  apimapper_onboarding({})

tools.name: apimapper_diagnose
tools.description:
Validate a token + siteUrl pair before profile creation. Runs token decode, identity probe (WordPress then Joomla fallback), iss/site-URL match (anti-phishing), capability check, scope check, and a subject-binding check (whoami) that flags a key whose record is not bound to an existing user before it hits the server's key_unbound_subject deny. Returns ready=true/false plus structured blockers[] and a recommendation.

Example:
  apimapper_diagnose({ token: 'amk_live_eyJ2IjoxLC...XYZ.abc123', siteUrl: 'https://example.com/wp' })

siteUrl.description: Site URL the token is meant for (e.g., "https://example.com/wp")

tools.name: apimapper_render
tools.description:
USE THIS when the user asks to 'visualize', 'show as diagram', 'render', 'draw', or 'display as a table/chart/flow' — produces deterministic, pre-formatted text output (tables, flow-diagrams, charts, schema-trees, json-tree, diffs). Prefer this over manually composing ASCII art in your response: the output is drift-free and consistent across renders.

Render data as a ready-to-display text visualization (tables, diagrams, trees, charts, diffs). Returns text the user can read directly in any MCP client.

Prerequisite: fetch the data first with the appropriate source tool, then pass the result as 'data':
  - type:'table' | 'chart-bar' | 'chart-line' | 'json-tree'
      → use apimapper_connection_data / apimapper_advanced_read({ tool: "apimapper_graph_preview", arguments: {} }) /
        apimapper_advanced_read({ tool: "apimapper_flow_trace", arguments: { id } }) first
  - type:'flow-diagram' → use apimapper_advanced_read({ tool: "apimapper_flow_get", arguments: { id } }) first; pass the flow object
  - type:'schema-diagram' → use apimapper_advanced_read({ tool: "apimapper_schema_profile", arguments: { nodes, edges, target_node_id } }) first
  - type:'diff' → fetch both datasets, pass as { old: ..., new: ... }

Pure function: deterministic, no network, no side-effects. The returned text is ready to show as-is. You are also free to enrich it however your client allows — artifacts, inline images, diagram-markdown, charts — whatever renders best for the user.

Example:
  apimapper_render({ type: 'flow-diagram', data: flowObject })

data.description: Data to render. Shape depends on type — see description. A JSON-encoded string is auto-parsed; a plain string renders as-is.

title.description: Optional title shown above the visualization

columns.description: Field whitelist for table. Default: auto-detect.

mask_secrets.description: Mask values for sensitive field names in diff. Default true.

tools.name: apimapper_list_profiles

instructions:
## Critical rules (read first)

- Most tools are reachable via the gateway: apimapper_advanced({ tool: "<name>", arguments: {...} }). The arg key is `arguments` (NOT `input`). Omit `arguments` to discover a tool's schema.
- If a call returns "Unknown tool", it is gateway-only — wrap it as apimapper_advanced({ tool, arguments }).
- Verify connectivity with apimapper_health({}) — it is first-class in tools/list (call it directly, NOT via the gateway). Recover auth/config errors via apimapper_diagnose; deeper guidance via apimapper_get_skill({ topic }).
# API Mapper

Bridge any REST API into YOOtheme via a saved flow (Source → Filter → Transform → Output). One server, one Bearer key, 22-tool surface; 59 more behind `apimapper_advanced` (write/mutate) and `apimapper_advanced_read` (read-only); 81 total.

## How to use this MCP server

API Mapper is a three-layer gateway server. 22 tools are first-class in `tools/list`; everything else (59 more) is routed behind two gateways:
- `apimapper_advanced({ tool, arguments })` dispatches the write/mutati

## Available skill topics

For deeper guidance on specific aspects of API Mapper, call:
  apimapper_get_skill({ topic })

Available topics:
- getting-started — Quickstart, common tools, common pitfalls
- oauth — Wiring OAuth-protected sources (Google, Pexels, Instagram, Notion, ...)
- yootheme — Publish flows as YOOtheme sources; Save-vs-Publish
- joomla — Joomla 3-tier auth, com_ajax envelope, system plugin layout
- troubleshooting — HTTP status triage, flow issues, credential states
- render — Render a flow as a diagram (viz-type, flow-diagram output)
- jmespath-pitfalls — The 9 traps + date-primitive functions (date_weekday, date_iso_to_time, date_iso_to_date, time_in_window) + depth-cap warning
- jmespath-cookbook — Copy-paste JMESPath recipes (ternary, join, conditions, sort_by, coordinates, format_number, dates, two-transform split) + a GIBT-ES-NICHT list (arithmetic/split/regex/if-else) with workarounds; iterate via apimapper_advanced_read({ tool: "apimapper_jmespath_test", arguments: { expression } })
- merge-two-sources-on-key — Joining two sources on a shared key, including date-primitive bridging for weekday-name ↔ ISO-datetime joins
- conditional-style-multi-items — Per-row YOOtheme styles driven by a row field (text_color, panel_style)
- library-template-discovery — Inspect a library template's contract before activating
- yootheme-source-to-builder-handoff — Bind a published flow into a Builder element. Two shapes: field_mappings (fresh element; binding_for_flow → element_bind_source; map_item, bindingLevel) AND the theme-canonical #parent repeater form to dynamize an EXISTING designed layout (swap source.query.name to apiMapperFlow<Id>List; _condition '!'/'!!'; named-section discovery; article-context width)
- dynamize-existing-layout — READ FIRST when the customer says "keep the design exactly as it is" / "bind onto my existing section/page": ONE call does it — template_summary (find the named section) → binding_for_flow (source name + flat fields) → yootheme_builder_page_generate_dynamic({ layout_id, output: "new_page", etag, section_name, list_source_name, leaf_map, page: { title, published: true } }) → visual row check. The tool copies the subtree byte-identically and swaps only leaf_map names by construction (insert nothing, rebuild nothing)
